After verifying the necessary stability criteria, IMO codes were followed for the assessment. The following criteria from the International Code on Intact Stability 2008, Part B, Chapter 2.2.4 [3] were applied: - 2.2.4 Intact stability criteria - 2.2.4.1 The area under the righting lever curve up to the angle of the maximum righting lever should not be less than 0.08 meter radians - 2.2.4.2 The static angle of the heel due to a uniformly distributed wind load of 540 Pa (wind speed 30 m/s) should not exceed an angle corresponding to half the freeboard for the relevant loading condition, where the lever of wind heeling moment is measured from the centroid of the windage area to half the draught - 2.2.4.3 The minimum range of stability should be 20° for L ≤ 100 m In addition to the wind loads defined in 2.2.4.2, current, wave, and CEC-derived loads have been evaluated. Ice accretion was also considered (only for stability purposes). After checking for relevant criteria, IMO codes were followed (International Code on Intact Stability 2008, Part B, Chapter 6.3.) [3], which considers an additional load of: • 60 kg/m2 for horizontal surfaces • 15 kg/m2 for vertical surfaces • Increase of ice due to discontinuous surfaces according to percentages indicated 5.1 Loading Conditions A range of different loading conditions have been considered that could represent every situation expected regarding stability. These conditions are considered the most demanding ones. 16 different conditions have been analyzed and listed hereunder. 1. Transport condition without jack-ups 2. Testing condition towed/moored before ballasting w/o environmental loads 3. Testing condition towed/moored after ballasting with environmental loads, direction fore-aft 4. Testing condition anchored before ballasting w/o environmental loads 5. Testing condition anchored after ballasting with environmental loads, direction 90° 6. Testing condition anchored after ballasting with environmental loads, direction fore-aft 7. Testing condition anchored after ballasting with environmental loads, direction aft-fore 8. Survival condition anchored after ballasting w/o environmental loads 9. Survival condition anchored after ballasting with environmental loads, direction 90° 10. Survival condition anchored after ballasting with environmental loads, direction aft-fore 11. Testing condition anchored 2 Lines before ballasting w/o environmental loads Final Technical Report 23/57 12. Testing condition anchored 2 Lines after ballasting with environmental loads, direction fore-aft 13. Testing condition anchored A-frame before ballasting w/o environmental loads 14. Testing condition anchored A-frame before ballasting with environmental loads, direction fore- aft 15. Transport condition with jack-ups 16. Transport condition with jack-ups + ice Stability analysis results show that every loading condition widely fulfills the stability criteria, while the most restrictive loading condition is the last one, 16. Transport conditions with jack-ups + ice, due to having the highest center of gravity (amongst other reasons), still comply by a broad margin.
